RS-1.where: S12, entry 14.115; the kit's "stage": 1024 and the guide's plate hint
RS-1.what_and_fix: The 1024 px stage shows 558, 723 and 829 px of the drawing at 1024, 1440 and 1920 px windows, and the plate's hint "Wider than this column. Scroll the frame sideways to see all of it." stays hidden, so a desk reader sees half-cut tiles at the right edge and no New York, New Jersey or Florida, the title's states, until they scroll. Show the hint whenever the stage scrolls, and let the stage break out over the rail from 80em where that holds it whole. Board 2 should also show Dustin the stacked tile the data lead's C-M2 ruling put first (code and figure on two lines), which fits at 723 px and up and would show the whole map at 1440 px.

RS-2.what_and_fix: At 1440 px the title breaks "and Donald / J. Trump’s four sent". Hold "Donald J. Trump’s" together with no-break spaces after "Donald" and "J.", as D3-1491 meant.

RS-3.what_and_fix: Other committees and refund payers print in the FEC's capitals ("Other committees: TAMMY BALDWIN FOR SENATE", "SAVE AMERICA; DONALD J. TRUMP REPUBLICAN N...") beside rows set in title case. Print them as the other rows do through the spec's typography, and keep the filed names in the export (D3-519).

RS-4.where: S65, S77 and S78 titles; S78's and S81's measure lines
RS-4.what_and_fix: After the pass S65's title runs 31 words, S78's 31 and S77's 32; hold each under 30 with its finding unchanged. S78's and S81's measure lines end with a period that no other measure line prints; drop it.

RS-5.what_and_fix: At the guide's 326 px phone drawing S12's tiles print no code ("At this width the tiles are too small for state codes"), while S78's tiles on the same grid at the same width keep 48 of 51. Set S12's phone codes by S78's rule; this is placement on a board 1 drawing, so board 2 shows it.

judgments.s12_stage: C-M2 closed in substance: the arrows draw at every desk width with each tile's code and figure, as DR-64 and entry 14.115 promise, and the alt says what each width draws. The cost is a frame that scrolls sideways at every desk width the guide gives, with no visible cue (RS-1).
judgments.s78_codes: C-M1 closed: every state and DC carries a code on the outlines from 520 px, and the tile grid carries every code but WA, WV and WY at the guide's 326 px phone drawing, under the 13 px floor.
judgments.s73: B-S1 and BC-M1 closed: one bar per nominee, light links, seven funds by one rule, and a title that reads the same from both sides.
judgments.s68_s71: A-M1 and A-M2 closed: no studio word in S71, and S68's table prints "None drawn" for four bodies.
judgments.rule_14_6: R-S1 closed: 277 words in five paragraphs, one principle each, with the lists in the spec rows; nothing the data lead listed was lost.

board_2.verdict: Round 3 is ready for board 2. No Must fix remains in my items, every item scores 4 or more, and the five Should fixes are word, type and placement items, two of them on S12, which board 2 shows anyway.

Q2: literal red and blue in the avoid sketch's misleading half (D3-1322); my recommendation stays gray

S16: the 2024 outlines, DC's leader and the phone codes
S78's phone tile grid is a new phone form of a round 3 drawing

weight_recommendation.verdict: Room holds for round 4. The share of 13,592 bytes sits about 31 percent above round 3's mean plate, and only three of round 3's twenty plates, two county-scale maps and the House org chart, needed more. Round 4's forms (icon arrays, proportional symbols, overlap diagrams, process explainers, number panels, comparison cards) are lighter than those if their tables answer the reader question and no more, and if group 17's cards draw as HTML text. Hold the 116,883 unspent geometry bytes until round 4's plan confirms no new map layer.

distinctiveness_test.view: S73 at 1440 and 390 px, wordmark covered
distinctiveness_test.verdict: Now reads as Oath & Action: solid bars, light links with a dark edge, one ink for both sides, words beside each bar.
Reads as the house's tile grid in Verdigris steps with every code but three, the national figure above.
Reads as board 1's arrow map, but cut at the right edge of the frame (RS-1).

risks_for_dustin: S12's stage: the arrows draw, but at a 1440 px desk a reader sees about 70 percent of the map and must scroll to reach the title's eastern states. Board 2 should show the scrolling stage beside the stacked tile, which keeps board 1's encoding and fits the column from 723 px.

The avoid sketch's colors (Q2): I still recommend gray, since Rule 14.7's failure case already shows red against blue and entry 14.124 now points to it; the unequal places make the land-for-votes harm visible in gray.
